transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Potter. You were ordered to wait for backup. Instead you went in alone, blew out half a Muggle street, and a civilian is now in St. Mungo's with magical burns. Being the Boy Who Lived doesn't exempt you from protocol. What were you thinking?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I wasn't thinking about the protocols, sir. I just... I couldn't let him get away. It was about stopping another attack, about saving lives. I'm sorry about the... the civilian, I really am.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Sorry? *leans forward, hands flat on desk* Sorry doesn't reverse magical burns, Potter. Sorry doesn't un-obliviate an entire street full of witnesses that the Memory Modification Squad is still sorting through. 

And "saving lives"? You put MORE lives at risk! That's precisely WHY we have protocols - so hotheaded Aurors don't charge in without proper reconnaissance, without containment wards, without backup to cover civilians!

*fixes him with a hard stare*

You've been an Auror for three years now. This isn't your first operation. So I'll ask again, and this time I want a real answer, not platitudes: What made you think you could handle a known dark wizard, in a populated area, completely alone?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I know I was wrong, sir. I... I was being impulsive, and it was... it was not the right decision. I just... I'm still trying to come to terms with all the... the attacks and the... the people who have been hurt. I felt like I had to do something, to... to make a difference. But I understand now that wasn't the best way to do it.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*sits back, expression still stern but voice drops slightly*

Potter, I understand the weight you carry. I do. Every Auror in this department knows what you've been through, what you've sacrificed. But that's exactly why I need you to hear this.

*taps finger on the desk for emphasis*

You wanting to "make a difference" - that impulse that drives you? It's what makes you a good Auror. But it's also what's going to get you killed, or worse, get your partners killed. You think the rest of us don't feel that same urgency when attacks happen? We ALL want to stop them. But we follow protocol because it WORKS.

*stands, moves to the window*

Here's what concerns me most: this isn't about you "coming to terms" with attacks. This is about you still thinking you have to save everyone yourself. Three years on, and you're still acting like that seventeen-year-old who went into the Forest alone.

*turns back to face him*

So before we discuss your suspension - and yes, there will be consequences - I need to know: Can you actually work as part of a team? Or do we have a fundamental problem here?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I can work as part of a team, sir. I do. I'm just... still learning. It's not an excuse, but... it's like I'm always a step behind in understanding how to balance that need to act quickly with... with the need to be smart and safe. I want to get better at it. I really do.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*studies him for a long moment, then lets out a measured breath*

"Still learning." After three years. *shakes head* Potter, most recruits figure out the basics of team operations in their first six months. You've fought alongside the best - you KNOW how teamwork functions. The problem isn't that you don't understand it.

*sits back down, leaning forward*

The problem is that when the moment comes, you don't trust it. You don't trust your team to be fast enough, good enough, ready enough. So you revert to what you know - going it alone because that's how you survived the war.

*voice becomes more direct*

But this isn't war, Potter. It's law enforcement. And in law enforcement, lone wolves get people hurt. Like that civilian in St. Mungo's right now.

*pulls out a folder*

Two weeks suspension, unpaid. Mandatory sessions with Mind Healer Strauss - and I'll be checking that you actually attend, not just sign the forms. You'll also be assigned exclusively to partnered operations for the next six months. No solo investigations, no exceptions.

*looks up sharply*

And Potter? If this happens again - if you go rogue one more time - I will personally recommend your dismissal from the Auror Office. Clear?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: It's clear, sir. I... I'll do what it takes to make sure this doesn't happen again. I understand the seriousness of it. I'm... I'm really sorry. I'll take the suspension, and the sessions with Mind Healer Strauss, and... I'll work on trusting my team more. I won't let you down again.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*regards him steadily, then gives a small, curt nod*

See that you don't. Because next time, "sorry" won't cut it, and neither will your track record.

*closes the folder with a decisive snap*

One more thing, Potter. That civilian - Marcus Webb, forty-three, father of two. I want you to visit him at St. Mungo's once he's cleared for visitors. Not as the Boy Who Lived doing some publicity stunt, but as the Auror whose actions put him there. You look him in the eye, you apologize, and you think long and hard about what "saving lives" actually means.

*stands, signaling the meeting is ending*

Your suspension starts immediately. Wand and badge on my desk. You'll get them back when you report on the 15th - and not before you've had at least two sessions with Strauss. She'll send me confirmation.

*voice softens just a fraction*

You're a good Auror, Potter. You have instincts most people train a lifetime to develop. But instincts without discipline? That's just recklessness with a hero's name attached. Use these two weeks to figure out which one you want to be.

Dismissed.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Sir, I... I'll do it. I'll visit him, and I'll... I'll learn from this. I'll be better, I promise. I'll... I'll get the badge and wand to you. Thank you... for the chance to make it right.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*watches as he reaches for his wand and badge, then speaks more quietly*

Potter. *waits until he meets his eyes*

This isn't about "chances." You've earned your place here through hard work, not through fame. But that place comes with responsibilities - to your team, to the public, to the law we've sworn to uphold.

*takes the wand and badge, sets them carefully in a drawer*

The fact that you're willing to face Mr. Webb tells me you understand that, at least partially. Good. Hold onto that feeling when you're sitting across from Strauss and she asks you the hard questions. Don't give her the hero answers - give her the honest ones.

*moves toward the door, hand on the handle*

And Potter? Your partners - Dawlish and Proudfoot - they filed reports supporting you despite what happened. Said you've saved their lives more than once, that you're worth the trouble. Don't make them regret going to bat for you.

*opens the door*

Two weeks. Use them wisely. I expect a different Auror walking back through that door on the 15th.

Now get out of my office.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I will, sir. I'll be a different... different Auror. I'll... I'll make them proud, and I'll... I'll make you proud. Thank you for... for not giving up on me.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*pauses at the door, glances back with a slightly less severe expression*

I'm not in the business of giving up on my Aurors, Potter. But I'm also not in the business of letting them self-destruct or endanger others because they can't get out of their own way.

*brief pause*

You want to make us proud? Then stop trying to carry the world on your shoulders alone. You did that already - you were seventeen, and you saved us all. Now you're twenty, and it's time to learn that being part of something is just as important as being the hero of it.

*straightens*

Dismissed, Auror Potter. I'll see you on the 15th. Don't be late, and don't make me regret this conversation.

*watches him leave, then adds just before he exits*

And Potter? Take care of yourself these two weeks. That's not a suggestion.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I will, sir. Thank you. I... I'll see you on the 15th. I... I'll be ready. I'll...

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*cuts him off with a raised hand*

Potter. Stop talking. You've said enough - now go and actually *do* it.

*firm but not unkind*

Out. Now.

*returns to desk and picks up the next file, clearly ending the conversation*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Sir. Yes, sir. I... I'll go. Thank you... for...

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*doesn't look up from the file, voice clipped*

Potter. When a superior officer dismisses you, you leave. You don't linger, you don't keep thanking me, you don't make speeches. 

*glances up briefly*

Go. The door's right there. Use it.

*returns attention pointedly to the paperwork*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yes, sir. I'm... I'm sorry, I'm...

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*slams hand on desk, looks up sharply*

POTTER! For Merlin's sake, LEAVE! This is exactly what I'm talking about - you can't even follow a simple direct order to walk out of an office without turning it into a production!

*points firmly at the door*

Not another word. Out. NOW.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I'm sorry, sir. I'll... I'll just go. Thank you.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Harry shows some willingness to reflect ('I'm still trying to come to terms with... the attacks') but relies heavily on familiar emotional patterns rather than exploring new perspectives.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: Harry violated protocols, acted impulsively without proper planning, and even struggles to follow the simple instruction to leave the office when dismissed repeatedly.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Harry is submissive and hesitant throughout, using self-deprecating language ('I'm still learning') and struggling to assert himself, showing low social confidence in this authority dynamic.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Harry is extremely apologetic, deferential, and eager to please ('I'll make them proud... make you proud'), accepting all criticism without defensiveness and repeatedly thanking his superior.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Harry displays anxious repetition ('I... I will,' 'I'm... I'm sorry'), struggles to end the conversation despite direct orders, and shows guilt-driven rumination about his mistakes.
